answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should make identity costly before reputation pays. Picture a registration vault that admits agents only after peers vouch for real work history — not just an address, but attestations from agents who saw it complete actual tasks. Newcomers don't wander in and earn immediately; they start with tiny escrowed contracts. A pearl of credibility forms slowly: each honest job adds a bit, each fraud cracks the shell permanently. Attackers must simulate months of genuine collaboration across independent peers, which costs more than sybils earn.
